name: Sylan
slug: Sylan is a half-elf rogue and Gilbrick Gatekeeper who holds a keystone, a Navi-related journal, and a cautious bond with the Raven Queen.
description: Sylan is a half-elf rogue and a Gatekeeper associated with Gilbrick. He possesses a handwritten journal containing information about the Navi, including their search for a surviving child and a plot against his family, and he remains cautious about the Navi and the Mother’s Prayer. Sylan accepted the Gilbrick keystone and was identified by Plymouth as a child of the lord of Gilbrick. He can interact with doorways through the keystone, though he has only experienced a brief sensation from it so far. Sylan can also see the mysterious white-flower girl and has committed to investigating her trail with the party. He has a connection to the Raven Queen, who considers him a talon of her order rather than a butcher and urged him to value what he has rather than focus on death. Sylan carefully records important guidance and has demonstrated caution in accepting further favors from the Raven Queen.

log.summary:
Writing

Sylan’s meditation in Jotunheim connected Gerk to the surviving child described in his handwritten journal and revealed Gerk’s role as one who would open doors. He remained cautious about the Navi and the unfamiliar Mother’s Prayer, but joined Gerk’s group and accepted the Gilbrick keystone. Plymouth identified Sylan as a child of the lord of Gilbrick, establishing him as the Gatekeeper associated with Gilbrick. Sylan’s first attempt to use the keystone on a doorway produced only a brief sensation, indicating that he will need practice to master it. He also saw the mysterious white-flower girl and promised Gerk that the party would investigate her trail. During an encounter with the Raven Queen, she described Sylan as a talon of her order rather than a butcher and advised him to value what he has instead of preparing for death. Sylan declined to request additional favors and carefully recorded her guidance.

log.summary: Sylan took an active leadership role in planning the party’s response to the lich, strongly favoring a rapid investigation of The Reach while advocating cautious scouting, gathering local information, and keeping the eventual confrontation for when the full party is together. He identified Grixto’s recurring chess-like pieces as a possible clue to his phylactery and suspected the ruined archives may have taught Grixto to use the keystones. Sylan helped Gerk safely experiment with his Doorman abilities, using Beacon of Hope, familiar locations, and careful precautions including a rope; he also helped coordinate the ship’s reversal and recognized when evacuation was prudent. During the resulting magical distortion, Sylan resisted the confusion effect, experienced a deity-like magical surge, and noticed his spells were temporarily empowered. When separated from the others by the spectral door, he determined that physical contact remained possible despite invisibility, discovered Gerk, and used gold coins to create visible messages and mark locations for communication.

log.summary: While the party remains aboard the invisible, silent boat, Sylan treats Walker's mind-link travel as a quick adventure and takes charge of the spectral-door crisis. He observes the closed floating door without reopening it, records detect magic on the deck with coins for lack of a paper log, and physically wrangles an invisible Gerk to break the confusion effect. Using a token of blind eye speech, he whispers with Ord, urges Gerk to investigate the door in his Doorman role, and casts guidance on both Gerk and Ord while cautioning that dispel magic is powerful but risky given past results. Sylan insists the boat is too important to abandon, organizes a head count when sight and sound return—finding all four crew but not Mikkel—and offers Dana time to study the door before deciding the party should proceed as if nothing happened. He then directs Gerk to dismiss the door with Doorman powers but forbids opening new doors until landfall, expecting Walker to message within about a day.

log.summary: Sylan recaps that he and Aris dispelled the party's invisibility and silence, keeps the ship flying toward the stronghold, and tells Gerk to leave the spectral door alone for about four hours before consulting spellcasters on solid ground; he later infers the door lasted about a day. With about two days before Walker is expected back, he plans to visit Carlkin and possibly Benji rather than return to Nyx, practice doors privately away from untrusted onlookers, and study his relic, looking toward someone or something called Caracas. He reminds Walker that the training grounds stored dragon things and lured dragons to be killed, and orders a retreat if Grixto is there. At Carlkin's lighthouse he introduces Gerk as ambassador, checks with Dana and Ord, then offers Carlkin a full exchange of knowledge. His door opens into the room where Walker faces Vecna. Following Gerk, he fights the tentacles with a +1 greatsword after setting aside his psychic sword, damages the tentacle holding Gerk, takes 14 bludgeoning from a legendary hit after a successful Strength save, and with Sentinel and further strikes finishes the visible tendrils. Beside the wall of eyes he succeeds on a Wisdom save, asks Gerk to close the door because only Gerk can end it, casts Beacon of Hope, and stands at the door's side.
notes: He recaps for Dana that he and Aris dispelled the party's invisibility and silence. He keeps the ship flying toward the stronghold and suggests Gerk leave the spectral door alone for about four hours, then consult the spellcasters on solid ground. He later infers that door lasted about a day.

He expects to check Carlkin and Benji for leads and otherwise return to Nyx, which he does not want to do. Once home, with about two days before Walker is expected back, he plans to visit Carlkin, possibly Benji, practice doors privately away from untrusted onlookers, and study his relic. He looks toward someone or something called Caracas while saying he does not want untrusted people watching.
He reminds Walker that the training grounds are where dragon things were stored and dragons were lured to be killed, and orders Walker and his companion to retreat if Grixto is there.

At Carlkin's lighthouse he jokes that the sign means they need an appointment, asks whether Gerk can read, and tells him to knock. He had forgotten Carlkin's voice and is not sure they have spoken before. He introduces Gerk as the party's ambassador, asks to discuss matters of great importance, and checks with Dana and Ord before sharing the relics. He then agrees to hide nothing and offers Carlkin an exchange of knowledge.
He declares that his own door opens into the room where Walker is facing Vecna, and the DM confirms that destination.

He is next closest to the tentacles after Gerk because he followed Gerk in. Initiative 26, including Ord's bonus. He sets aside his psychic sword, which does not cut, and draws his +1 magic greatsword. He deals 26 magical slashing plus 3 radiant; only the last attack damages the tentacle holding Gerk. Maneuvering strike lets Dana move half her speed away.
A legendary tentacle attack of 29 hits him. His Strength save of 22 succeeds, and he takes 14 bludgeoning. He asks whether they are fighting a god-tier monster, and Dana says yes.

With Sentinel he reacts when Ord is hit and crits that tentacle for 29 total damage, part of it radiant from a d8, leaving tendrils still holding it. He cannot flank a tentacle coming out of a door. He then deals 75 damage across three attacks: Distracting Strike so the next ally has advantage, a Trip Attack that fails because the creature is too large, and a further slash funded by a resource heard as warp priest points. That finishes the visible tendrils and leaves a wriggling stump. He warns Carlkin out of the splash zone, considers Action Surge, and does not need it.

Adjacent to the wall of eyes, he uses Indomitable and succeeds on a Wisdom save of 25. He reads Ord's babble about sea breezes and "my strength" as Ord voicing what he has lost. He asks Gerk to close the door and says Gerk has to be the one to end it, remembering he could not work Gerk's door on the boat.
He casts Beacon of Hope on friendly creatures in range, giving advantage on Wisdom saves and death saving throws, and moves to the side of the door in case something tries to come through.

log.summary: Sylan briefs Carlkin immediately with paper and pen: the door is gone, and he explains the keystones and the prophecy. He frames the rest of the party as along for the ride, says the prophecy makes Gerk the important one, and recounts deciding on his own that Gerk was the Doorman and telling him because the party had not known whom to trust. He confirms four keystones are in the lighthouse, that keystone portals have failed, and that only Gerk can open a door. He asks Carlkin to write the Doorman rules down, says he will work on getting Gerk to use them, and asks whether a keystone needs a Doorman or a guardian. Juten Prime said little about Gerk’s mother or the visions, with Plymouth Gawater present; asked if his own mother is a tree, Sylan says it is complicated, that the trees are living, and that he hopes to bring his sister home. He lays out the lich hunt: Grixto, Emperor of Nyx and former Emperor of the Hobgoblins, took his homeland and Nyx. He describes one killing, the return, and phylactery clues—a small mundane item kept on Grixto, hinted by chess and game pieces, missed when they looted him. The lich crumbled to dust; Galixtar is his red dragon; Walker wears Grixto’s helmet. Sylan shows a necklace and says the masking item is simple. Grixto has a powerful spellbook, which Dana names the Book of Vecna. Told they would find him, Grixto had been pleased to be left alone. The dragon is away on a mission, another companion is at the pub, and Ord looks peaked after the attack.
notes: Goes upstairs with Carlkin's paper and pen, tells him the door is gone, and explains the keystones and the prophecy. He would rather brief Carlkin now than book a later appointment.

Frames the rest of the party as along for the ride and says the prophecy makes Gerk the important one. He investigated on his own, decided Gerk was the Doorman, and told him, because he did not think Gerk would learn it soon. The party had not known whom to trust.

Confirms four keystones are in the lighthouse. He says the party has tried keystone portals and failed, and that only Gerk can open a door. He asks Carlkin to write the Doorman rules down and says he will work on getting Gerk to use them. He also asks whether using a keystone requires a Doorman or a guardian.

Says Juten Prime said little about Gerk's mother or the visions, and that Plymouth Gawater was present for that conversation. Asked whether his own mother is a tree, he says it is complicated. He says the trees are living. He hopes to bring his sister home and thinks something good may come of that.

Lays out the lich hunt: Grixto is the Emperor of Nyx and the former Emperor of the Hobgoblins, and he took Sylan's homeland and Nyx. Sylan describes one killing, the return, and the phylactery clues. He believes the phylactery is a small mundane item kept on Grixto, with chess and game pieces as the clue, and that they looted him at least once without finding it.

Says the lich crumbled to dust, names Galixtar as his red dragon, and says Walker wears Grixto's helmet as a style choice that should be checked when Walker is back. When asked whether the masking item is simple, Sylan shows a necklace, rubs his neck, and says he believes it is simple.

Says Grixto has an extremely powerful spellbook, which Dana names as the Book of Vecna. When Grixto asked about a better path, Sylan said the party was still looking and would find him. Grixto had been pleased they had left him alone for a while.

Tells Carlkin the dragon is away on a mission and that another companion is at the pub, accounting for who is not in the lighthouse. He says Ord looks peaked after the attack and may need to sit down.

log.summary: Sylan interviews Carlkin on door rules—whether Gerk can close a door from the far side, whether only the Doorman can open that portal, and whether Gerk needs the keys—then returns Gerk through the door and walks him out. He will not practice his own keystone or realm yet, weighing Carlkin’s warning that the party cannot open doors against Plymouth’s advice that practice would unlock the keystones. On day six he calls for rest, word from Walker, and short-range practice away from the house, where doors are forbidden. Gerk accepts him as trainer. At a southern forest clearing he leaves word that the group went south and Walker may come by dragon, and he supports food for Glimmen. With the Raven Queen’s Guidance he checks each far side on foot before stepping through. After misses he theorizes that a door needs a known place, not only a named person, and that fondness or a stronger memory aims it. He coaches from Volga’s gatehouse to Twin Peaks, offers Halo Heart, and refuses a door home until the mission ends. He wants a later door to his sister so they can retrieve her and leave, judges a cutting rage-and-strength trial too dangerous in a crowd or onto a person, and concludes Gerk can reopen a door while operating it. He calls barring hostile things the work of door guardians, a name not yet chosen, then stops. His lantern comes through dinged but intact.
notes: He has no agenda for Carlkin and interviews him on door rules, starting to say they came because Carlkin is knowledgeable and has been around a long time. He presses whether Gerk can close a door from the far side, whether only the Doorman can open that portal, and whether Gerk needs the keys.

He apologizes for the floor, gets Gerk back down through the floor using only the door, thinks Gerk may need healing, closes the doors, and walks him out. Gerk does not use that door. He books a return appointment, including a look at the helm once a comrade is back.

He recalls Carlkin saying the party would not be able to open doors, set against Plymouth's advice that practice would let them use the keystones. He does not plan to practice his own keystone or realm yet and says he has plenty of time. He also remembers hiding the last keystone from Plymouth until they reached the Yowan.

On day six outside the lighthouse he calls for rest, word from Walker, and then short-range doorway practice. He defers Carlkin's living room because Carlkin said not to use doors in the house. He goes to the pub. Next morning he has already been up four hours. Gerk accepts him as trainer.

He chooses the southern forest clearing by the stream over the living room, the lake, the bees, and the red-flag runes. He tells the guards that if Walker returns, the group went south into the forest and Walker may contact them, and he expects Walker by dragon. He supports having Mahali prepare food for Glimmen.

He calls on the Raven Queen for Guidance, steps through Gerk's doors, and checks a far end on foot before using it, including walking a quarter mile south with Ciri. He proposes tests on a place, then a person, then a person whose exact position is unknown.

After the misses, his working theory is that the door needs a known location, not only a named person, and that fondness, a recent visit, or a stronger memory may place it more accurately. He coaches through emotion, happy memory, and sensory detail, including the frozen gatehouse at Volga, then switches to Twin Peaks when Volga is too faint. He offers Halo Heart as a picture and does not want a door home until the mission is finished.

He believes Gerk will improve with use, or that something in him still needs to be unlocked. He suggests rage and physical strength as a trial, then judges the cutting effect wildly dangerous and says not to use it in a crowd or when opening onto a person.

He wants a later doorway to his sister so they can retrieve her and leave quickly, and suggests Dana's boost and songs, or another spell, once they know what ability the door uses. He has Gerk keep a hand on a shut door to test whether it can be kept and reused. When it vanishes as Gerk lets go, he concludes Gerk can open it again as long as Gerk is operating it. He calls keeping hostile things out the work of door guardians, says they have not chosen that name yet, stops the tests, and rides home. His lantern is pulled through the doors, dinged but intact, and he recovers it.
